investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm", indicating the peer-pod VM quota on those nodes is fully consumed. The other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also ruled out: no lower-priority victims were found on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completed, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail entirely.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because no evidence was produced.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's node affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are at capacity. If the selector were broadened or additional kata-capable nodes were added, scheduling could succeed.

TERTIARY — Insufficient number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in the cluster: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the required extended resource, providing a narrow scheduling target with no headroom for concurrent eval probes.

QUATERNARY — Concurrent remote-agent workloads (e.g., real user agents or other eval runs) holding all peer-pod VM slots, causing transient exhaustion at the time of the eval run. This would be a transient capacity issue rather than a permanent misconfiguration.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-27 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) before it can poll state, the pod scheduling failure prevented agent creation entirely, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated and causing the contract validation to fail.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots across the two eligible nodes, and the remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. No preemption victims were available. As a result, every attempt to schedule a peer-pod VM for a remote agent during the eval window was rejected by the scheduler after ~124–147 seconds, preventing agent creation and making it impossible for the state-polling eval to collect any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent VM pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definitions. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is scoped to the observability eval.

possibleCauses: Most likely — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing peer-pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This directly matches the scheduler message in failed-check.message and all three sibling check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at capacity, no scheduling is possible regardless of preemption.

Tertiary — peer-pod VM leak or stuck termination: previously created remote-agent VMs may not have been cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new allocations. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is intended to release resources, but a prior failed or interrupted run could leave VMs unreleased.

Lower confidence — cluster autoscaler not configured or unable to add kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in time: the scheduler message 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling' and zero preemption victims suggest no autoscaling occurred during the ~147s window.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm", indicating the peer-pod VM quota on those nodes is fully consumed. The other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also ruled out: no lower-priority victims were found on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completed, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail entirely.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because no evidence was produced.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's node affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are at capacity. If the selector were broadened or additional kata-capable nodes were added, scheduling could succeed.

TERTIARY — Insufficient number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in the cluster: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the required extended resource, providing a narrow scheduling target with no headroom for concurrent eval probes.

QUATERNARY — Concurrent remote-agent workloads (e.g., real user agents or other eval runs) holding all peer-pod VM slots, causing transient exhaustion at the time of the eval run. This would be a transient capacity issue rather than a permanent misconfiguration.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-27 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) before it can poll state, the pod scheduling failure prevented agent creation entirely, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated and causing the contract validation to fail.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots across the two eligible nodes, and the remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. No preemption victims were available. As a result, every attempt to schedule a peer-pod VM for a remote agent during the eval window was rejected by the scheduler after ~124–147 seconds, preventing agent creation and making it impossible for the state-polling eval to collect any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent VM pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definitions. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is scoped to the observability eval.

possibleCauses: Most likely — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing peer-pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This directly matches the scheduler message in failed-check.message and all three sibling check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at capacity, no scheduling is possible regardless of preemption.

Tertiary — peer-pod VM leak or stuck termination: previously created remote-agent VMs may not have been cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new allocations. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is intended to release resources, but a prior failed or interrupted run could leave VMs unreleased.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-27 because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pods remained stuck unscheduled until the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing the expected-output contract entirely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, while the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out before the VM is provisioned, preventing the eval runner from reaching the agent creation, state polling, or runtime chat steps. Because the pod never schedules, no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is ever collected, and the expected-output contract is violated in full. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage, though the same scheduling path would affect real remote-agent provisioning requests.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 144s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which is the step that submits the pod — scheduling failure here prevents all downstream evidence collection

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the observed latencyMs=147830 is well under the outage threshold, so the feature-level outage gate has not been crossed by this check alone, but the two required sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) also failed
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the extended peer-pod VM slots are fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no allocatable capacity for new eval pods. All three sibling checks hit the same error, confirming this is not a single-pod anomaly.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 kata-capable nodes. If the affinity rules have become overly restrictive (e.g., a label was removed from nodes after a node pool update), effective capacity is further reduced.

Tertiary — cluster node pool under-provisioning: the 2 kata-capable nodes may not have been scaled to meet concurrent eval demand, especially if multiple eval runs or real workloads are competing for the same vm slots simultaneously.

Lower probability — pod resource request or limit set too high relative to available vm quota per node, causing the scheduler to report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm even when slots nominally exist.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the 2 eligible nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Use cluster tooling (e.g., kubectl describe node) to read the allocatable and requests fields for kata.peerpods.io/vm on each node that carries the resource. Compare against the number of running peer-pod workloads.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect node labels on all 6 nodes to verify affinity/selector alignment
reproductionSteps.details: Check whether the 4 nodes that did not match the pod's node affinity/selector are missing expected labels (e.g., a kata or peer-pods capability label) that would make them eligible for scheduling.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling layer (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: All three remote-agents eval checks failed with identical Unschedulable messages citing kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion and node affinity mismatch. The scheduling layer is the earliest violated boundary, blocking all downstream agent lifecycle steps.

affectedAreas.label: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool on the 2 eligible cluster nodes
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the only 2 nodes that carry this resource, indicating the VM slot quota is fully consumed.

affectedAreas.label: Node affinity / node selector configuration for remote-agent pods
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 nodes were excluded by the pod's affinity/selector, concentrating scheduling onto the 2 kata-capable nodes and amplifying the capacity shortage.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — remote-agent probe branch
affectedAreas.reason: The createAgent call at line 1918 submits the pod that fails to schedule. All evidence collection is downstream of this call, so scheduling failure produces a fully empty evidence object and a complete contract violation.

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: All 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) and the message assertion ('hello from aura') are unmet because the pod never starts.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check the current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and in-use counts on the 2 eligible nodes to determine whether the resource pool is still exhausted.
If vm slots are exhausted, identify which workloads are holding them and determine whether any can be terminated or whether the node pool needs to be scaled up to add more kata-capable nodes.

Audit the node affinity/selector rules on remote-agent pods against the current label set on all 6 cluster nodes to confirm whether the 4 non-matching nodes are intentionally excluded or have drifted from the expected label configuration.
Re-run the three remote-agents eval checks after any remediation to confirm recovery and collect the expected evidence fields.

Consider adding a pre-flight cluster capacity check to the eval runner that reports available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before attempting pod creation, so future failures surface a more actionable message than a raw scheduler error.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false in infra/evals/status/features.json (line 185), so this check alone does not trigger a feature-level outage gate; however, the two required sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) also failed, which may satisfy the degradedAfterFailures=1 threshold defined at line 187.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduling failure is still present or was transient. A pass would produce all 5 required evidence fields and the 'hello from aura' assertion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run all three remote-agents sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the shared Unschedulable failure pattern persists across all three checks, confirming a cluster-wide capacity issue.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on all cluster nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly measures whether the vm resource slots are exhausted. If allocatable equals zero or all slots are consumed by running pods, resource exhaustion is confirmed.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node labels and pod affinity/selector spec for remote-agent pods
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the 4 non-matching nodes are excluded by design or by label drift. If labels are missing that should be present, node affinity misconfiguration is confirmed as a contributing factor.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Review cluster events for kata.peerpods.io/vm pods in the production-api namespace around 2026-06-27T09:27–09:33Z
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Cluster events would show whether other workloads were consuming vm slots at the time of the eval run, confirming contention, and whether any pods were eventually scheduled after the eval timed out.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of the remote-agent-runtime probe that returns all 5 required evidence fields and passes the 'hello from aura' assertion would disprove that the cluster is currently capacity-constrained.

kubectl describe node output showing available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes would disprove resource exhaustion as the cause and shift focus to a pod spec or API error.
A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state while remote-agent-runtime continues to fail would disprove the shared-scheduling-bottleneck hypothesis and suggest a check-specific issue.
Evidence that the 4 non-matching nodes do carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource but are excluded only by an intentional affinity rule would disprove the node-label-drift hypothesis.
Cluster event logs showing the pods were eventually scheduled (after the eval timeout) would suggest a transient queue delay rather than hard capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the cluster before attempting agent creation, alerting when available slots fall below a safe threshold.

Add a cluster node-label conformance eval that verifies all expected kata-capable nodes carry the required labels for remote-agent pod affinity, catching label drift before it causes scheduling failures.
Add a historical trend eval that tracks remote-agent pod scheduling latency over time, enabling detection of gradual capacity erosion before hard exhaustion occurs.

Consider a canary eval that submits a minimal remote-agent pod with a short timeout specifically to test scheduler responsiveness, decoupled from the full agent lifecycle, to isolate scheduling failures from runtime failures faster.
